title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (header 'n° 391', p. 15), photographed upside down. It was evidently reused as scrap paper, which is how it ended up in cote 14; the archive foliation '6v' appears in the margin. Its content is an early version of Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. V, §1 ('Hyperplans, chambres et facettes').

(1) It ends a paragraph on reflections in parallel hyperplanes. If s and s' are reflections with respect to parallel hyperplanes H and H' (same direction, same vector part), then s'(x) = s(x) + 2t. Substituting s(x) for x gives s'∘s = translation by 2t. When K = R and Φ is positive definite, ||t|| is the Euclidean distance between H and H'.

(2) Section 5, 'Chambres dans un espace affine', sets up the topology:
- A finite-dimensional real affine space E receives the topology of R^n via any choice of origin.
- This topology is independent of the origin, because translations are homeomorphisms.
- For a hyperplane H and a nonempty connected set C disjoint from H, C lies in exactly one of the two open half-spaces. These half-spaces partition E − H into two connected open sets. The one containing C is denoted D_H(C).

(3) Lemma 1: if 𝔥 is a locally finite family of affine hyperplanes with union S, then:
- S is closed and nowhere dense (rare);
- each connected component C of E − S (a chamber) equals the intersection over H ∈ 𝔥 of the half-spaces D_H(C).

The proof begins as follows:
- S is closed, because a locally finite union of closed sets is closed (Top. gén. I, §1, n° 5, prop. 4).
- Each hyperplane is rare.
- Locally, only finitely many H_i meet a neighbourhood V of a point, and a finite union of rare closed sets is rare.

The page breaks off at the start of the proof of the equality C = ∩ D_H(C).

This serves the general theory of hyperplane arrangements, chambers and facets used for Weyl groups and affine Weyl groups in Bourbaki Lie IV–VI.
errors: Notational clash: the index range '(1 ≤ i ≤ n)' for the finitely many hyperplanes meeting V reuses n, the dimension of E. This is harmless, and the published version avoids it.
Grammatical slip in the typescript: 'une topologie bien déterminée pour lequel' should read 'pour laquelle'.
No mathematical errors. The proof is incomplete on this page because it continues on the next sheet of the draft, which is not in this folder.

ideas.what: Composition of reflections in parallel hyperplanes is a translation by twice the vector separating them.
ideas.modern_name: Reflections and translations in affine Weyl groups

ideas.what: Locally finite hyperplane arrangement: the union is closed and nowhere dense; each chamber is the intersection of the open half-spaces containing it.
ideas.modern_name: Chambers of a locally finite hyperplane arrangement

ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. V §1 (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused Bourbaki typescript draft of Lie ch. V §1 with standard, published content. It has no connection to the cycle-theory notes on the neighbouring pages and carries no Grothendieck annotation of mathematical substance.
transcription_corrections: The page is upside down. It is a Bourbaki typescript ('n° 391'), not Grothendieck's manuscript; the marginal '6v' is an archive foliation mark.
'pour lequel' is the original's wording (grammatically 'pour laquelle').
The ensemble of hyperplanes is typed as a doubly underlined H (Bourbaki's script/bold H), rendered as 𝔥 in the transcription.
